extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, editorial staff, reviewers, authors, and other scholarly-publishing professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the Council of Science Editors (CSE) White Paper guidance on roles, responsibilities, and ethical standards for participants in scholarly publishing (editors, reviewers, sponsors, authors, publishers), including misconduct, corrections, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and protections that preserve editors' independence to make publication decisions without inappropriate interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers scope of editorial autonomy, limits, and interactions with owners/publishers; full guidance located in the body of the white paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considering Appeals for Reconsideration of Rejected Manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and processes for authors to appeal rejection decisions and for editors to review such appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likely includes timelines, grounds for reconsideration, who reviews appeals, and documentation required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing Allegations or Findings of Misconduct (see section 3.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: How editors/journals should respond when misconduct is alleged or confirmed, with reference to the research-misconduct section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references the misconduct identification and response procedures in section 3.0 of the white paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint Servers
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and considerations for handling manuscripts that have been posted to preprint servers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May discuss preprint disclosure, citation, priority, and effects on peer review and journal policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations and obligations to keep manuscript content, reviewer identities (where applicable), and other confidential information secure during the editorial process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses what must be kept confidential, when confidentiality may be breached, and safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and management of conflicts of interest affecting editors, reviewers, authors, and other participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles for disclosure, recusal, and mitigation; cross-linked with Conflict of Interest Disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific requirements and formats for declaring financial or nonfinancial interests that could bias research or editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers what to disclose, where disclosures appear, and how journals should handle undisclosed conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation Manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards to detect and prevent inappropriate citation practices (e.g., coercive citation, citation stacking) that distort the scholarly record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examples and recommended editorial responses to suspected citation manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Board Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Roles, responsibilities, and expected conduct of editorial-board members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likely covers selection, duties (peer review, strategic input), conflicts of interest, and term limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of the Publication Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations and benchmarks for prompt handling of submissions, peer review, and publication steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include recommended turnaround times, monitoring, and transparency about typical timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errata, Retractions, and Expressions of Concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for correcting the literature, including issuing errata, retractions, partial retractions, and expressions of concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers when each instrument is appropriate, standards for notices, and linking/crossmarking corrected items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing Authorship Disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and principles for resolving disputes over authorship attribution and order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recommended steps (investigation, institutional involvement), documentation, and corrections to the byline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Critiques/Responses to Published Articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for acceptable critiques, responses, and letters to the editor about published work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May set boundaries for civility, evidence, novelty, and procedures for submission and assessment of critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and expectations for authorship eligibility and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies contributions that merit authorship and obligations associated with being listed as an author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributorship Models
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative approaches to recognizing contributions (e.g., CRediT) instead of or alongside traditional authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on implementing contributorship taxonomies and recording individual roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for acknowledging contributors who do not meet authorship criteria and for disclosing funding/support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes who should be named and how funding and other support are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for determining and reporting the sequence of authors on a byline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May address conventions, equal-contribution statements, and resolving disputes about order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to the Author Byline
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and approval steps required to add, remove, or reorder authors after submission or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually requires written agreement from all authors and, in some cases, institutional confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive list of obligations authors hold (e.g., data integrity, disclosure, approval of manuscript, responding to queries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses duties before submission, during review, and after publication (e.g., correcting the record).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and processes for choosing appropriate peer reviewers for manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes expertise matching, conflict checks, diversity of reviewers, and avoiding reviewers with competing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Responsibilities of Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected conduct of peer reviewers, including confidentiality, objectivity, and timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers declining review when conflicted, avoiding plagiarism of reviewed material, and providing constructive feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of Reviewer Impropriety
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative cases of unethical reviewer behavior (e.g., stealing ideas, biased reviews, coercive practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as warning signs and informs corrective actions and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Anonymous Reviewers: Critique of the Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the strengths and weaknesses of anonymous (single- or double-blind) peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores implications for fairness, accountability, and potential reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewarding Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and practices for recognizing or compensating reviewers for their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include acknowledgments, certificates, CME credit, or other incentives while guarding against conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor Roles and Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for sponsors (e.g., industry, funders) with respect to publication planning, authorship, data access, and disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses ethical conduct, process control, and transparency in sponsor–journal interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Planning (Sponsor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on appropriate involvement of sponsors in planning publications arising from sponsored research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers what is acceptable vs. unacceptable influence over content or journal selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship (Sponsor-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: How sponsor personnel should be credited and how sponsor contributions affect authorship decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes disclosure of sponsor contributions and avoidance of ghost authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process Control (Content and Journal Selection) by Sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards limiting sponsor control over manuscript content or choice of journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages editorial independence and full disclosure of sponsor involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Conflicts of Interest (Sponsor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for sponsors to disclose interests that could influence study design, analysis, or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of wider COI policies applicable to authors and funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to and Provision of Data (Sponsor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations that sponsors provide access to study data and not obstruct independent verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes data-sharing obligations and conditions under which data must be made available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright (Sponsor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies regarding copyright ownership and transfer when sponsors are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May address licensing, author rights, and sponsor claims to content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Registration and Dissemination of Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations to register clinical trials and to disseminate all results transparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers registries, timing of registration, and reporting negative as well as positive findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper Sponsor Conduct and Ethical Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: General expectations for sponsors to behave ethically in all aspects of publication and research dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes avoidance of undue influence, transparency, and adherence to journal and institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations between Editors and Publishers, Sponsoring Societies, or Journal Owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for healthy, transparent relationships between editorial leadership and the entities that own or sponsor journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses governance, checks on owner interference, and mechanisms for dispute resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Oversight Committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory or governance structures to oversee publication ethics and policy adherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role, composition, and powers of such committees to ensure integrity and handle disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities to the Media
rubrics_metrics.description: How journals and editors should interact with media about published research and corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes accurate communication, managing embargoes, and responding to media inquiries responsibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in Scholarly Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies to promote DEI across editorial boards, reviewers, authorship, and published content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include recruitment practices, bias mitigation, and measures to increase representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Research Misconduct and Guidelines for Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework for recognizing different forms of research misconduct and recommended journal actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces the misconduct section and ties to subsequent, more detailed subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistreatment of Research Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and examples of unacceptable treatment of human or animal subjects that may constitute misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on detection, reporting, and required remedial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falsification and Fabrication of Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and criteria for identifying data falsification or fabrication as misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers investigation steps and editorial responses, including corrections or retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Piracy and Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of plagiarism and other piracy of intellectual property, and policies for handling such cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes detection, author notification, and sanctions/corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Models for Responding to Research Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of national and international frameworks and bodies that handle research-misconduct claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how journals should coordinate with national bodies and follow legal/regulatory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Bodies Responding to the Problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of national organizations or agencies in investigating and adjudicating research misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May list examples of national bodies and their typical responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Research Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Authoritative definitions (and boundaries) of what constitutes research misconduct for journal purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies terms and differentiates misconduct from honest error or dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended procedures for investigating alleged misconduct, including roles, evidence handling, and confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes steps for preliminary assessment, full inquiry, and reporting outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Investigation Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions and considerations after an investigation concludes (corrections, retractions, notifying stakeholders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses communication, record-keeping, and follow-up monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Suspect Manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: How and when manuscripts suspected of misconduct should be reported, and to whom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtopics include reasons a manuscript is suspect and recommended reporting channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why Might a Manuscript be Considered Suspect?
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators and red flags that may render a manuscript suspect (e.g., data anomalies, plagiarism, image manipulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to triage and prioritize investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Might Notify a Journal about a Suspect Manuscript?
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential reporters of concerns (e.g., readers, reviewers, institutions, whistleblowers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes handling anonymous vs. identified notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Should be Done When Misconduct is Alleged?
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediate procedural steps a journal/editor should take upon allegation receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines preliminary assessment, communication with authors/institutions, and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whom Should a Journal Notify about a Suspect Manuscript?
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders and bodies that should be informed (institutional officials, funders, co-authors, readers) when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes confidentiality and legal considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Investigates Allegations of Misconduct?
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies whether the journal, the authors' institution, or national bodies are responsible for investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes coordination and division of responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Information Should be Provided During Investigations?
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of documentation and evidence journals should collect and share during an inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include manuscripts, raw data, peer-review histories, and correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Accusations from Anonymous Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for assessing and acting on anonymous allegations while guarding against abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains verification steps and weight given to anonymous tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Images and Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines specifically addressing manipulation or misuse of digital images in submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes detection techniques, acceptable adjustments, and consequences for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Handling Image Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for image acquisition, processing, reporting, and archiving to ensure integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable manipulations, required disclosures, and submission of original image data if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Handling Guideline Violations (Image/Data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stepwise process for addressing violations of image/data-handling guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include contacting authors, institutions, issuing corrections/retractions, and notifying readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting the Literature: Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of erratum, corrigendum, partial retraction, retraction, and expression of concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to choose the appropriate corrective instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting the Literature: Processes and Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and workflows for issuing corrections and maintaining the integrity of the scholarly record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers decision-making criteria, transparency, and permanent linking of notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of Errata, Partial Retractions, Retractions, and Expressions of Concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative cases demonstrating when and how different corrective notices are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides practical examples to guide editorial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Third-Party Inquiries about Scientific Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: How journals should respond to inquiries from media, legal counsel, federal agencies, and other third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes protocols for disclosure, referral to institutions, and legal considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media (Handling Inquiries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance for responding to media questions about alleged or confirmed misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes accuracy, avoiding premature statements, and coordinating with institutions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Counsel (Handling Inquiries)
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how to involve legal counsel in responses to misconduct allegations or third-party inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses risk assessment, confidentiality, and compliance with subpoenas or legal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Agencies (Handling Inquiries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for interacting with federal agencies that investigate research misconduct or regulate research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes notification expectations and cooperation protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix and Resources/Case Studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting materials, references, examples, and case studies illustrating application of the white paper's guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides practical examples and further reading; specific case studies are referenced throughout the table of contents.
